exact_rule.post_event_gain: The separate bounded consumer 0x10018fb40 loads segment Float32 gain at +0x68. If gain compares equal to 1 it skips multiplication; otherwise each returned Float32 sample is multiplied once by gain using FMUL (vector 0x100190ebc..ec8, scalar 0x100190ee8). Before the output writer y=RN32(x*g) under nearest-even arithmetic, with finite normal-or-zero operands and no underflow/overflow. The IEEE product sign applies to exact zero, including zero gain. This loop contains no clipping, mixing, gain ramp, FMA, or finite-value guard.
exact_rule.precision_boundary: Unit conversion is exact. Nonunity event multiplication can round; finite gain alone does not guarantee a finite normal output. The conditional equation permits either sign of finite normal gain and signed zero; the retained numerical gain controls exercise six positive values. A candidate must separately reject overflow/nonfinite results and define denormal/FP rounding behavior for any bit-equivalence claim. Arbitrary converter gain is not promoted to the unit-conversion theorem.
